title: Structured log ingress gateway with dynamic schema adapters and correlation propagation
creator: Priya Rao
description:
Goal: Build a resilient, multi-tenant structured log ingress gateway (onramp) that normalizes heterogeneous log payloads into a canonical schema, preserves/propagates correlation IDs and trace links, and forwards to Loki/ELK backends with backpressure handling and tenant routing.

Scope:
- HTTP/GRPC ingestion endpoints supporting JSON and ndjson streams.
- Pluggable schema adapter chain to map vendor-specific fields into a canonical observability schema (timestamp, level, service, env, trace_id, span_id, tenant_id, message, attrs).
- Correlation ID enrichment: extract from common headers (traceparent, x-request-id, x-correlation-id) and attach to log JSON when missing.
- Tenant-aware routing: route to tenant-specific Loki tenants or to centralized ELK pipeline based on metadata and config.
- Backpressure and batching: implement adaptive batching with request-level timeouts and circuit-breaker when downstream is degraded.
- Lightweight validation: reject malformed JSON with clear error codes; metric emission for rejection reasons.

Out of scope for initial rollout:
- Full field-level rewriting for private on-prem customers (follow-up ticket).
- Long-term archival / cold storage routing.

Acceptance criteria:
- 99th percentile ingestion latency from client to gateway < 120ms under normal load.
- Correlation IDs present for > 99.5% of enriched events for supported header patterns.
- Gateway properly routes > 95% of tenant-tagged traffic to dedicated tenant backends in staging.
- Error rate for malformed payloads < 0.1% and emits descriptive metrics.
- Automated e2e test harness and staged rollout via console flags.

Rollout plan:
1. Deploy gateway to staging with canary traffic (~1% production) and enable schema adapter in warn-only mode (do not rewrite fields).
2. Validate correlation propagation and routing by replaying recorded traffic and running smoke dashboards.
3. Gradually increase traffic and turn on active normalization for supported app teams.
4. Run a 72-hour stability window, monitor ingestion latency, error budget burn, and tenant routing correctness.
5. Post-rollout retrospective and follow-up tickets for edge-case field mappings.

Telemetry & Dashboards:
- Ingestion gateway SLO dashboard: latency percentiles, throughput, active connections.
- Error dashboard: parse failures, rejected payloads by reason, schema adapter mapping failures.
- Correlation coverage dashboard: percent of logs with trace_id/span_id per service.
- Tenant routing metrics: routed-by-tenant counts, routing failures, fallback occurrences.

Risk & trade-offs:
- Normalizing fields at the gateway simplifies downstream consumers but may mask original vendor fields; we will keep raw payload in a raw_key for 30 days to enable debugging.
- Schema adapter complexity requires ongoing maintenance; start with small set of vendor adapters (nginx, envoy, python-logging, k8s kubelet) and iterate.
- Additional CPU cost for enrichment and validation; mitigate by using a small C++/Rust core for hot-path parsing and offloading heavy transforms to worker pool.

Implementation notes:
- Use an internal ingress service (ingress-v2) as a new container behind existing LB.
- Schema adapters implemented as WASM filters to allow safe sandboxing and hot-reload.
- Persist correlation extraction heuristics in config and expose via Console for ops to modify without deploy.
- Emit structured telemetry to internal metrics topic and tag all metrics with gateway_version and adapter_version.
